items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: And then when he met up with Bayshade up there again, that was it. Because several days she wouldn't see him when she would call to find out he was somewhere with Bayshade.

ctx.x: one of those things. I don't think anybody ever mentioned, not that we're, we try to specialize in

the way it is. Well no, I mean it's just the way it is. Yeah, it's just facts, it's just the way it was. That was the thing with his claim, where when he had gone back to New York and he had begun drinking again, and after he was told that it was detrimental to him and he would continue that it was short in his life. So his wife had told me, well there's nothing she could do, that's just the way he took it. Yeah, well it's hard to say. And then when he met up with Bayshade up there again, that was it. Because…

Yeah, it's hard to say. I think about Baby Dodds and Johnny Dodds. I guess you didn't know the Dodds brothers, do you remember them? I don't remember them. I knew of them after they left. I knew them both in Chicago. Johnny never took a drink in his life hardly and Baby was quite a drinker. Yeah. Johnny died when he was 48 and Baby kept drinking and drinking and the other he lived to be 65 or so. That's right. Doesn't usually really kill him, but it might make it a little worse if they have that stroke. Maybe he…
